goals.rationaleEn: Seedling and yeast cases independently require observation-based life-characteristic reasoning; non-observation is not misread as absence.
Plant leaf and animal intestine cases each test the cell-tissue-organ-organism relation with concrete part-whole reasons.
Two distinct microscope sets cover plant, animal, and bacterial cells while separating visible evidence from supplementary model claims.
Leaf and root-cell models require structural and functional assignment; the root case tests the limit of assuming chloroplasts in every plant cell.
Mitochondrial and chloroplast scenarios separately test the model and its explanatory limits; historical uptake is not claimed as directly observed.
A three-form classification and a data-poor algae case test organization criteria and justified uncertainty.
A newly constructed bilayer and a rotated, channel-lacking section test lipid orientation, selective pathways, and model limits.

The second application case reverses salt concentration but asks only for water direction. The current goal requires renewed reasoning about both particle diffusion and osmosis under changed conditions; a second independent demonstration of both is missing.
